doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Roots of his music: Thompson Methodist Church and classical records
summary: His musical roots were in the church and a wind-up gramophone with classical records; his mother was musical, his father not.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I want to get some sense of the early sense of music or where the roots of your music talents, in the sense that: was it the family? Was it in Thompson Methodist Church, where you used to go?
Yeah, that’s it. Thompson’s Church. Thompson’s Methodist Church . . .
. . . was the church, yeah. I had forgot the name of it.
Where do you trace those roots?

The roots, really, for the music and everything else, actually came from the church – basically from the church. Of course we did have – I guess you call it a graphophone [sic: gramophone] that then you wind up. It had a horn and you had records. We had records of classical music.
Yes, yes. We had records of – I can’t remember the names of some of the classical people at that time, but we could hear all that type of music.
What about your mother and father? Were they musically inclined?
My mother was. My father wasn’t.
